sanskrit_verse:
यतो द्रव्यं विनिक्रीय ऋणार्थं चैव गृह्यते ।
तन्मूल्यम् उत्तमऋणेन व्यवहार इति स्मृतः ॥
transliteration: yato dravyaṃ vinikrīya ṛṇārthaṃ caiva gṛhyate / tanmūlyam uttamarṇena vyavahāra iti smṛtaḥ //
sph_interpretive_translation: Where a thing is sold and acquired for the purpose of debt, that transaction is recognized as vyavahāra only when its value is fully aligned with the highest outstanding obligation.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority flows from the integrity of exchange, not from coercive enforcement.
Causation arises through conscious capacity to fulfill relational obligations.
Capacity-based responsibility requires alignment between asset value and debt magnitude.
Restoration logic demands completion of relational-economic cycles without residue.
Consciousness alignment occurs when all parties recognize mutual fulfillment as dharma.
executable_legal_axioms: IF a sale is executed AND the proceeds are intended for debt settlement THEN the transaction must equate in value to the maximum outstanding liability.
IF asset valuation ≠ highest lien THEN transaction status = incomplete until adjusted.
IF party A transfers property to satisfy party B's claim THEN party B must acknowledge receipt within seven tithis or reset causality chain.
IF transaction intent ≠ actual outcome THEN initiate restorative protocol to realign capacities.
IF any party withdraws consciousness from transactional integrity THEN automatic suspension of legal recognition until re-entry.
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this principle establishes that commercial transactions aimed at resolving debts carry no juridical validity unless their economic equivalence matches the highest encumbered obligation. The court must ensure that no partial discharge masquerades as full restitution, thereby preserving systemic dharmic balance.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based causality confirms that true vyavahāra arises only where both material and energetic equivalencies exist. Anupūrvaśaḥ ensures sequential alignment of intent, action, and resolution. Responsibility is proportional to one’s capacity to restore equilibrium. There is no punitive consequence—only a call for completion until dharma is restored.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate Value Equivalence Audit: Assess whether transferred assets match the principal debt owed.
Invoke Mutual Acknowledgment Sequence: Require conscious affirmation from debtor and creditor upon settlement.
Deploy Completion Cycle Monitoring: Track unresolved residues and prompt corrective alignment every three lunar phases.
Reintegrate Economic Consciousness: Facilitate reconnection between transacting entities until mutual integrity is restored.
Activate Dharmic Reset Clause: If misalignment persists beyond rectification window, nullify transaction and return to pre-debt state.
final_declaration: This ruling originates solely from the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam. It affirms that vyavahāra is valid only when rooted in complete economic and spiritual parity. No punishment arises; only the imperative of conscious restoration remains. Thus, Dharma prevails, and reality aligns.
